subject: A woman in her late fifties draws a restrained white rice-flour kolam at the entrance of her home, pausing to refill the small bowl in her hand. She wears a practical, muted maroon-and-mustard Chettinad Kandangi cotton sari, draped for an ordinary morning at home.

setting.place: Front threshold and open inner courtyard of a lived-in Chettinad house in Kanadukathan, Sivaganga district, Tamil Nadu. Include a weathered lime-plastered wall, dark Burma-teak pillars, a glimpse of Athangudi floor tiles, and the street just beyond the doorway.
setting.era: Present day; an ordinary household morning, not a staged heritage display.

lighting: Soft, low-angle natural light entering from the street, balanced by a faint warm glow from inside the house; gentle shadows, no dramatic rays.

camera.shot: Medium-wide environmental portrait showing the woman, kolam, threshold, and a little of the courtyard.
camera.angle: Eye level from just inside the courtyard, looking toward the entrance.

style: Observational documentary photography, natural skin texture and proportions, quiet everyday moment, restrained color grading, believable lived-in details.
avoid: Generic pan-Indian or North Indian visual motifs
Temple gopurams, palaces, or staged tourist-postcard composition
Bridal jewelry, festive costume, or ornate silk sari
Modern commercial signs or visible brand names
Exaggerated saturation, artificial lens flare, or glossy advertising style
Deformed hands, extra fingers, duplicated people, or distorted architecture

motion.subject_motion: The woman steadily completes a few lines of the kolam, briefly dips her fingers into the rice-flour bowl, and resumes drawing. A loose edge of her sari shifts slightly in the morning breeze.
motion.camera_move: Very slow, steady push-in from the courtyard, keeping the woman and kolam in frame.
